Some questions about domestic use of VPNs

1. Well the client would be the web browser if you're using it on a computer. I use mine to surf the web under an alternate IP for security and anonymity.
  2. It depends on the IP configured to your VPN software and the connection from your router to their router and servers. Paid VPNs will generally be a lot more secure and faster than free ones but I use free VPN software and VPN servers that are compatible for the Mac platform so it's a little bit different. I've never tried Netflix but I assume it will be fine if streamed via a VPN. May be a bit slower as it has to take an extra route to get to your router and then to your computer/device via the network interface card (NIC).
  3. My router is an all-in-one router (the brand is Netgear) you buy from an electronic/tech shop so it has a firewall, routing table etc. (I don't really know myself). It functions like a regular router you'd buy for LAN usage and for connecting to the Internet.
  4. Yes but that's life. If you're going to use a VPN it will be slower than normally sending a request to and from your own router and to another server in an alternate location to your house/office. But maybe a VPN that you purchase online may be better than this (I don't really know as I've never payed for a VPN).

I'd obviously recommend considering a paid VPN service so you are guaranteed security, privacy and performance benefits but if that's not an option, there are quite a few free VPN services out there. Myself and the other users would be more than welcome to suggest some for you.

Hope I helped!

1.) How frequently would people like these challenges to run? I think monthly would work best for most of us busy people.

2.) As far as competition goes, if we want it to be competitive, how do we feel about using a voting system based on Voat's comment ranking?

3.) As far as constraints go, I think we could start off by designing a game around a theme or a mechanic, or the combination of the two. I think it would be totally fine for submissions to be in any form, whether it's a game design doc or an actual game.

4.) Is this something people would legitimately like? I'd personally love to see this become a regular thing, but it only works if people want to participate.

Ultimately, I think it could lead to some very cool collaborations and conversations involving game design, which will hopefully make us all better designers every challenge.
